In biology , a monotypic taxon is a taxonomic group ( taxon ) that contains only one immediately subordinate taxon. [ 1 ] A monotypic species is one that does not include subspecies or smaller, infraspecific taxa. [ contradictory ] In the case of genera , the term "unispecific" or "monospecific" is sometimes preferred. In botanical nomenclature , a monotypic genus is a genus in the special case in which a genus and a single species are simultaneously described. [ 2 ]
